claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has a single-phase BCC structure.
The asymmetric XRD peaks in the baseline alloy arise from dendritic versus interdendritic micro-segregation.
The baseline alloy has a room-temperature fracture strain significantly below theoretical expectations.
Approximately 4 at.% Cr is to be added to the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces a complex multicomponent cubic C15 Laves phase with AB2 structure.
The Cr-induced Laves phase is Hf2Cr or a closely related phase.
The Laves phase occupies approximately 4 vol% of the modified alloy.
The Laves phase forms a reticulated, interconnected network at grain boundaries and interdendritic regions.
Annealing above approximately 900 °C but below the Laves-phase solvus promotes Laves-phase nucleation.
A controlled cooling rate preserves the reticulated Laves-phase morphology.
Cr solute causes a significant contraction of the BCC lattice parameter.
The reticulated Laves-phase network impedes crack extension through crack deflection and crack bridging.
Atomic-size mismatch and electronegativity differences associated with Cr generate severe lattice distortion in the BCC matrix.
Cr-induced lattice distortion increases the Peierls stress and produces solid-solution hardening.
Lattice-parameter contraction demonstrates successful Cr incorporation and Laves-phase stability.
The fracture-strain response to Cr is non-monotonic and depends on whether the Laves phase is reticulated, isolated, or excessively interconnected.
A BCC lattice contraction greater than 0.03 Å allows solid-solution hardening to dominate and may recover fracture strain toward theoretical values.
The baseline alloy fails prematurely through micro-segregation-induced void coalescence.
The mechanism requires a BCC lattice contraction greater than 0.02 Å and a Laves-phase volume fraction of approximately 4 ± 1%.

The proposed Cr concentration series, with identical thermal processing and measurements of matrix Cr, lattice parameter, phase morphology, and fracture strain, can distinguish micro-segregation effects from Cr-specific phase formation.

contradictions.description: The lattice-contraction criterion is inconsistent: solid-solution hardening is associated with a shift greater than 0.03 Å, the boundary requires greater than 0.02 Å, and falsification uses greater than 0.01 Å as the definition of a measurable contraction.

The boundary states that isolated Laves particles cause the proposed mechanism to fail, but the falsification rule treats isolated particles accompanied by unchanged or degraded fracture strain as falsifying. That outcome is instead consistent with the stated boundary condition and therefore is not discriminating.
